sentences.text: Libanopristis was a cartilaginous fish belonging to the class Chondrichthyes.
It is a member of the family Sclerorhynchidae.
A single female specimen preserved with nine embryos inside offers early fossil evidence of ovoviviparity in batoids.
The genus was first described by Hay in 1903.
The species was originally described as Sclerorhynchus hiram and later renamed Rhinobatus eretes before being placed in the genus Libanopristis.
Libanopristis lived during the Cenomanian stage, between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
This extinct genus lived in Lebanon during the Late Cretaceous period.
